description:
## What the code does

Two methods take optional booleans and `Option<&[&str]>` property selectors as positional parameters rather than via a typed Params struct:

`calendar_event_parse` at crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event_parse.rs:14-18:

```rust
pub async fn calendar_event_parse(
    &self,
    blob_ids: &[Id],
    properties: Option<&[&str]>,
) -> Result<CalendarEventParseResponse, ClientError>
```

`principal_get_availability` at crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/principal_availability.rs:18-25:

```rust
pub async fn principal_get_availability(
    &self,
    principal_id: &Id,
    utc_start: &UTCDate,
    utc_end: &UTCDate,
    show_details: Option<bool>,
    event_properties: Option<&[&str]>,
) -> Result<PrincipalGetAvailabilityResponse, ClientError>
```

## What idiomatic Rust would do

The canonical mail-client `email_parse` at crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/email.rs:299-303 takes a typed Params struct:

```rust
pub async fn email_parse(
    &self,
    blob_ids: &[Id],
    params: Option<EmailParseParams>,
) -> Result<EmailParseResponse, jmap_base_client::ClientError>
```

Where `EmailParseParams` (mod.rs:253-282) is:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Default, serde::Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct EmailParseParams {
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub properties: Option<Vec<String>>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub body_properties: Option<Vec<String>>,
    // ... more optional fields ...
    #[serde(flatten, default, skip_serializing_if = "serde_json::Map::is_empty")]
    pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
}
```

The Params-struct pattern lets the implementation:

1. Add new spec-defined optional args without breaking call sites (struct fields are non-positional).
2. Honor the workspace extras-preservation policy via `#[serde(flatten)] extra` — already mandatory for in-scope method-argument structs per workspace AGENTS.md.
3. Use `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` to omit absent fields uniformly via one `serde_json::to_value(&params)` call rather than five hand-built `if let Some(x) = ...` blocks at every call site.

## Why it matters

1. **Vendor extras are blocked.** Workspace policy mandates `extra: serde_json::Map<...>` on method-argument structs (workspace AGENTS.md, "Extras-preservation policy" → in scope: "Method-argument structs in *-client crates"). Neither `calendar_event_parse` nor `principal_get_availability` has any way to thread vendor extras into the wire request — `extra` doesn't exist because the struct doesn't exist. The two methods are *the only two* method APIs in the crate without a vendor-extras path.

2. **Future spec arg additions break the API.** When the calendars draft adds (say) a `fetchPart` argument to `CalendarEvent/parse` — and IETF drafts routinely add such arguments through revision cycles — the only available shape is to add another positional parameter, breaking every call site. A Params struct absorbs the change.

3. **Canonical-template divergence.** mail-client's parse path uses `EmailParseParams`. Per workspace AGENTS.md canonical-template rule, calendars-client should mirror this shape. The divergence is unjustified by spec content (the calendars draft's parse method is structurally analogous to mail's).

4. **bool-positional smell on principal_get_availability.** The 5-positional-arg shape forces callers to write `sc.principal_get_availability(&pid, &start, &end, Some(true), Some(&["summary"]))` — five positional args with two `Option`-wrapped bools/slices is exactly the "bool param that should be in a struct" smell from the /review-rusty type-design section. A reader at the call site has no clue what `Some(true)` controls.

## Fix shape

Add two Params structs in calendars-client mod.rs:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Default, serde::Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct CalendarEventParseParams {
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub properties: Option<Vec<String>>,
    #[serde(flatten, default, skip_serializing_if = "serde_json::Map::is_empty")]
    pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Default, serde::Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct PrincipalGetAvailabilityParams {
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub show_details: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub event_properties: Option<Vec<String>>,
    #[serde(flatten, default, skip_serializing_if = "serde_json::Map::is_empty")]
    pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
}
```

Update method signatures to take `Option<CalendarEventParseParams>` and `Option<PrincipalGetAvailabilityParams>` respectively. Method bodies flatten the struct via the same idiom canonical mail-client uses (email.rs:314-325):

```rust
if let Some(p) = params {
    let pv = serde_json::to_value(&p).map_err(|e| { ... })?;
    if let serde_json::Value::Object(map) = pv {
        for (k, v) in map { args[k] = v; }
    }
}
```

Pre-0.1.0 breaking change; cheap to apply now, costly later.

- crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/email.rs:299-329 (canonical email_parse with EmailParseParams)
- crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mod.rs:249-282 (canonical EmailParseParams definition)
